doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage on work songs, church and social life
title: The Natchez dance hall fire and Cage's first wife
summary: They discuss the fatal fire in Natchez, which Cage says was 1919, when his first wife died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Let's, let's cut it off for a minute so you can get a little beer. That might be good for your throat, huh? I think they're out there. Yeah, I think it's working now. We're talking about in church you used to play. I used to play. Remember that hall point up in Edmonton, Mississippi? Jefferson Hall. Well, I know about that. I never was there. I heard of Walter Barnes and a friend of mine used to play with Walter Barnes, but he wasn't there that night and I thank the Lord for that. Oh, that's good.
Well, about 250 people got put up in there and I got mad in there in 1919. My first wife died. You know that song about that? You know they had a song about that? No, I never did know it.
Well, they had one about called the death of Walter Barnes and they had one called, wasn't that an awful day in Natchez?
Yeah, well that's the place I'm at now. I belong to that church. I stayed there I don't know how long. I was baptized in the Mississippi River there.
